subject.title: build(deps): bump the actions group across 1 directory with 14 updates

question: Should OpenClaw accept this grouped set of new privileged GitHub Action revisions after the mechanical guard fixes?
rationale: These revisions execute with repository tokens, secrets, publishing permissions, security-report access, or agent credentials, so accepting their upstream code is an owner security choice that mechanical tests cannot settle.

options.title: Review and accept batch
options.body: Audit the upstream revisions, repair the four stale assertions, refresh exact-head checks, and merge the grouped update.

options.title: Split sensitive updates
options.body: Separate token, Docker publishing, CodeQL/SARIF, and Codex action bumps into smaller independently reviewed PRs.

options.title: Hold current pins
options.body: Pause this batch and retain the existing revisions until owners are ready to complete the supply-chain review.

recommendation.title: Review and accept batch
recommendation.body: Audit the upstream revisions, repair the four stale assertions, refresh exact-head checks, and merge the grouped update.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the exact workflow guard invariants and is the strongest individual history-backed owner for coordinating the grouped automation update with the security CODEOWNERS team.
